line: In business. French equipment maker Schneider Electric is buying factory software firm P T C. Regulators still have to approve the deal.
In security. Hackers posing as A I firm an-thropic's staff sent malware to A I policy experts. Researchers tie the hackers to China's government.
In manufacturing. Chip giant T S M C is reported to plan another price rise next year. Demand for its newest chips is said to outrun supply.
In robotics. Germany is paying for tens of thousands of drones, built in Ukraine. Each hunts down Russian attack drones; the exact number is not yet given.
In new models. N-vidia-backed start-up Reflection is said to be readying an open A I model. Open means anyone can run it; nothing has shipped yet.
In health. A Stanford team had thirty seven thousand A I agents read old drug trials. The agents found a clue to safer drugs; no lab has tested it.
In daily life. McDonald's reportedly uses A I to set menu prices in America. It calls the tool optional; some store owners say they feel pushed.
And something lighter. Munchy's Pizza, a Florida family shop, promised never to use A I. The promise drew tens of thousands of people online.
Also in the full report. I B M says its quantum chip beat a supercomputer in one test. A I gun turrets are said to guard Kyiv from drones.
And for the bigger picture: hopes for A I prop up tech shares. Yet U S borrowing costs are the highest since two thousand two. Watch if they stay this high; the A I rally depends on that.
